Tier.label: Party level
Tier.hint: Changes damage for traps with “Damage ignores party level” unticked (SRD severity table). DCs stay as written.

pit.name: Hidden Pit
pit.text: A plank lid covered with dirt gives way under weight. A slightly sagging floor gives it away. Athletics wedges the lid shut.
pit.flavor: The floor gives way — a black pit opens beneath!

spikedPit.name: Spiked Pit
spikedPit.text: A hidden pit with sharpened stakes at the bottom. The fall hurts twice: the impact and the spikes.
spikedPit.flavor: The floor collapses — spikes glint below!

bearTrap.name: Bear Trap
bearTrap.text: Steel jaws hidden under straw or leaves. A caught creature is held in place until freed with Athletics or thieves’ tools.
bearTrap.flavor: Steel clangs underfoot — the jaws snap shut!

poisonDarts.name: Poison Darts
poisonDarts.text: A pressure plate fires darts from hidden tubes in the walls. Tiny holes in the masonry give it away; the tubes can be plugged.
poisonDarts.flavor: Darts whistle out of the walls!

arrowVolley.name: Arrow Volley
arrowVolley.text: A tripwire looses a volley from arrow slits. Everyone in the area is under fire.
arrowVolley.flavor: A click — arrows rain from the slits!

scythingBlade.name: Scything Blade
scythingBlade.text: A heavy blade swings out of a slot in the ceiling and sweeps just above the floor. The slot and scratches on the walls give the mechanism away.
scythingBlade.flavor: A huge blade whistles down from above!

fallingNet.name: Falling Net
fallingNet.text: A net hangs under the ceiling; a tripwire drops it. Anyone caught is held until they work free.
fallingNet.flavor: A heavy net drops from the ceiling!

collapsingRoof.name: Collapsing Roof
collapsingRoof.text: The supports are sawn through, and a tripwire brings the ceiling down. Cracks and fresh dust on the floor are the warning.
collapsingRoof.flavor: The ceiling groans — stones rain down!

rollingBoulder.name: Rolling Boulder
rollingBoulder.text: A pressure plate releases a stone ball that thunders through the corridor and knocks everyone down.
rollingBoulder.flavor: A rumble grows — a boulder rolls down the corridor!

fireJet.name: Fire Jet
fireJet.text: Nozzles in the walls spray flaming alchemical oil. Soot around the holes and the smell of oil give it away.
fireJet.flavor: Flame roars out of the walls!

acidSpray.name: Acid Spray
acidSpray.text: A pressurized vessel sprays acid on whoever steps on the plate. The floor around it is pitted with burns.
acidSpray.flavor: A hiss — acid sprays into your face!

poisonGas.name: Poison Gas
poisonGas.text: A plate opens valves and the room fills with caustic gas. The GM may have the door slam shut.
poisonGas.flavor: Greenish smoke creeps out of the cracks!

sleepGas.name: Sleep Gas
sleepGas.text: A sweet-smelling gas puts everyone in the area to sleep. A sleeper wakes when damaged or shaken awake.
sleepGas.flavor: The air turns sweet, eyelids grow heavy…

lightningRune.name: Lightning Rune
lightningRune.text: An invisible glyph on the floor strikes whoever steps on it with lightning. Arcana or dispel magic disables it.
lightningRune.flavor: A rune flares underfoot — lightning strikes!

frostRune.name: Frost Rune
frostRune.text: A glyph of cold covers everyone nearby in rime. The floor near it is always a little colder.
frostRune.flavor: The rune flares blue and the air rings with frost!

thunderPlate.name: Thunder Plate
thunderPlate.text: A plate carved with a glyph answers a footstep with a thunderclap that knocks everyone nearby off their feet. It can be heard far away.

witheringSigil.name: Withering Sigil
witheringSigil.text: A dark sigil drains life from everyone on it and fills them with dread. Dangerous even for seasoned heroes.
witheringSigil.flavor: Shadows reach out of the sigil and cold bites to the bone!

alarmPlate.name: Alarm Plate
alarmPlate.text: Harmless, but it rings loudly: guards and monsters learn they have guests. The GM gets a notice.
alarmPlate.flavor: Somewhere above, a bell starts ringing!

App.dragHint: Click a trap to configure it, or drag it onto the map to place it there as a hidden region.
App.empty: Nothing found. Try another search or filter.
App.sceneEmpty: No traps on this scene yet. Drag one from the library onto the map.
App.searchSelectedHint: Selected tokens roll Perception against traps within their spot range (usually 10 ft) and in line of sight.
App.triggerHint: Sets the trap off on the selected tokens, or on everyone in the area if none are selected.
App.attempt: Try to disarm with the selected token
App.confirmDelete: Remove the trap “{name}” from the scene?
App.confirmDeleteCustom: Delete your trap “{name}” from My traps?
App.revealAllHint: Reveal every trap on this scene to players
App.hideAllHint: Hide every trap on this scene from players
App.mineEmpty: Traps you configure and save show up here. Open any trap in the library or on the scene, change what you need and press “Save to My traps…” — you’ll be asked to name it.
App.mineHint: Click a trap to configure it, or drag it onto the map. Use the pencil to rename it.
App.ideaHint: Opens a form in your browser

Hud.reveal: “{name}” is hidden from players. Click to reveal.
Hud.hide: “{name}” is visible to players. Click to hide.
Hud.noticed: “{name}” was spotted by {who}. Players can’t see it yet — click to reveal.
Hud.disarm: Disarm “{name}” with the selected token ({skill}, DC {dc}). Failing by 5 or more sets it off.

Chat.noTargets: The trap went off, but nobody is in the area.
Chat.disarmFail: {name} fails to disarm “{trap}” ({skill}: {total} vs DC {dc}). The trap didn’t go off — they can try again.
Chat.disarmTriggered: {name} slips ({skill}: {total} vs DC {dc}, failed by 5 or more) — “{trap}” goes off!
Chat.searchNoneGm: {name} searches for traps and finds nothing (Perception {value}).
Chat.rollDamageHint: Roll damage now without waiting for the remaining saves. It’s one roll for everyone.

Notify.gmOnly: Only the GM can do this.
Notify.noGM: A GM must be connected: traps are resolved on the GM’s side.
Notify.notDnd5e: Trap Library is made for D&D 5e: checks and damage won’t work in another system.
Notify.noticed: {name} spotted “{trap}”. Players can’t see it yet — decide in chat or with the button on the map.
Notify.otherScene: This trap is on another scene.

trapId.label: Based on
trapId.hint: The built-in or custom trap this one was made from.

icon.label: Icon
icon.hint: Font Awesome icon class, e.g. fa-solid fa-fire.

detectRange.label: Spot range, ft
detectRange.hint: Passive Perception and searches reach this far, counted in squares like the ruler: 10 ft means one empty square in between.

attackBonus.label: Attack bonus
attackBonus.hint: If set, the trap attacks against AC instead of forcing a save.

damage.label: Damage
damage.hint: A formula such as 2d10. Empty — no damage.

condition.label: Condition
condition.hint: Applied on a failed save or a hit.

sound.label: Sound
sound.hint: A built-in sound or a path to your own file.

flavor.label: Text for players
flavor.hint: Shown to players in chat when the trap goes off.

stops.label: Stops movement
stops.hint: A token that steps in stops there (pit, bear trap, net).

fixedDamage.label: Damage ignores party level
fixedDamage.hint: Untick to make damage grow with party level — the table on the right shows how much.

fxMode.name: Animations
fxMode.hint: Built-in animations always work. If Sequencer and JB2A are installed, their effects can be used instead.

chatMode.name: Who sees the trigger card
chatMode.hint: With “GM only”, the owners of targets still get the card when they need to roll saves.

passiveDetect.name: Passive Perception
passiveDetect.hint: A player character coming near a trap notices it if their passive Perception meets the detect DC.

detectSight.name: Spot only in line of sight
detectSight.hint: Walls that block sight and closed doors stop a character from spotting a trap — by passive Perception or a search.

triggerBy.name: Who sets traps off
triggerBy.hint: Traps can fire on player characters only, so the GM can move monsters freely.

mapButtons.name: Trap buttons on the map
mapButtons.hint: The GM sees an eye button on every trap: one click reveals it to players or hides it. Each GM has their own setting.

detectMode.name: When a character spots a trap
detectMode.hint: What happens when a Perception check (passive or a search) succeeds. You can also switch this on the On this scene tab.
detectMode.reveal: Reveal it on the map to everyone and whisper the player
detectMode.gm: Tell the GM who spotted it; reveal it to players by hand

saveRolls.name: Who rolls saves against traps
saveRolls.hint: Players: each target in the trigger card has a save button for the character’s owner (the GM gets it too, plus “Roll the rest”). Module: rolls right away. Characters without a player are always rolled by the module.
saveRolls.players: Players roll with a button in the card

damageMode.name: When trap damage is applied
damageMode.hint: On click: the GM sees in the card who takes how much and presses “Apply”. Right away: damage and conditions apply as soon as the check result is known.
damageMode.button: When the GM clicks “Apply” in the card
damageMode.auto: Automatically, once the result is known

Device.title: Device
Device.hint: Describe the trap in-world — damage, DCs and conditions update to match.
Device.controlled: Set by the device: changes when you change its settings.

Editor.title: Configure: {name}
Editor.name: Name
Editor.tiersFixed: Same damage at any party level: {damage}.
Editor.dragHint: You can drag the card onto the map.
Editor.placeHint: Places it hidden at the center of the view.

Name.title: Name your trap
Name.label: Name
Name.hint: This is the trap’s name in My traps and on the map.
Name.overHint: This trap was placed from your “{name}”. Update it or save as a new one?
